clue.text: Paint-box used to depict Narcissus, say?

definitions.meaning: a small case for carrying make-up, which is face paint
Narcissus, who fell for his own reflection, is a case study in self-admiration

explanation.surface: Someone asks what an artist's paint-box was used for in a picture of the mythical Narcissus.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: Narcissus is an example, a 'case', of conceit. 'used to depict' only joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A make-up box is a lady's cosmetics holder, and Narcissus embodies conceit, so he is a literal instance of self-love.

clue.text: Volume given a cover and binding

parts.note: a lid is a cover for a container

explanation.surface: A book is given a jacket and a binding.
explanation.walkthrough: The bookbinding picture misleads: 'binding' is the definition, meaning legally in force.
explanation.definitionFit: A valid contract is legally enforceable, so it binds the parties.

clue.text: East Coast tourist centre in which grandmother appears to flourish

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
a tucket is a trumpet flourish, as in Shakespeare's stage directions

explanation.surface: A resort on the American east coast where grandma seems to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourish' looks like 'thrive' but is a fanfare. 'in which' and 'appears to' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: The island off Massachusetts, once a whaling port, is now a popular summer resort.

clue.text: Book value put on one's estate

parts.note: to treasure something is to value it
one's read as I'S, I being one
an estate is land

explanation.surface: A book valuation is placed on someone's property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book value' is an accounting phrase, but 'Book' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's adventure novel of pirates and buried gold is a famous book.

clue.text: Very large stomach concealed by extremely comfortable clothes

indicators.note: concealed by says the stomach letters are hidden inside what follows
extremely asks for the letters at the extremes of comfortable

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing size label for very large
tum is informal for stomach

explanation.surface: A big belly is hidden under very comfortable clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like 'very' but takes the first and last letters of COMFORTABLE, C and E, which wrap OSTUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume is a set of clothes, an outfit.

clue.text: It's wrongly said to damage one's reputation

definitions.text: It's wrongly said to damage one's reputation

parts.words: It's wrongly said to damage one's reputation
parts.note: describes false spoken words meant to harm a person's good name

explanation.surface: A remark claimed to harm someone's reputation is misreported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly said' looks like a mistaken claim but describes false speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Defamation in spoken form, a false statement harming a person's standing.

clue.text: Hunting party shortly to drive off

indicators.note: shortly says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a shoot is a party that goes out hunting game birds

explanation.surface: A group of hunters is told briefly to leave in their vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like it means 'soon' but tells you to clip the last letter of SHOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooing someone means waving them away, chasing them off.

clue.text: Tough grass — find way in

indicators.note: in says the road abbreviation goes inside the grass word

parts.note: hay is dried grass
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A tough grass in which one must find a path.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardy plant or person is robust and able to endure harsh conditions.

clue.text: Even a lord collapses under too much pressure

indicators.note: collapses says the letters of even a lord fall apart and rebuild

explanation.surface: Even an aristocrat breaks down when stressed too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapses' looks like the lord's breakdown but rearranges EVEN A LORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Overladen means carrying an excessive load, weighed down by a burden.

clue.text: No fear doctor may feel a failure here?

definitions.text: No fear doctor may feel a failure here?

parts.words: No fear doctor may feel a failure here?
parts.note: an exclamation of defiant refusal, read literally as a doctor's patient lying dead

explanation.surface: A doctor with nothing to fear might nonetheless feel he has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No fear' is the refusal; a doctor standing over a corpse would feel he had failed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal, meaning that something will happen only if the speaker is killed first.

clue.text: Dance that may come to the boil?

definitions.meaning: a nineteenth-century square dance, a set of quadrilles

definitions.text: that may come to the boil?
definitions.meaning: people who lance, piercing a boil with a blade to drain it

explanation.surface: A dance that heats up until it boils over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come to the boil' suggests heating water; here it means arriving at an abscess with a lance.
explanation.definitionFit: The quadrille-style set dance bears this name, and those who pierce boils are, literally, lance-wielders.

clue.text: Notice faulty serve could be critical

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper, an advertisement

indicators.note: faulty says the letters of serve are wrong and must be put right in a new order

explanation.surface: A tennis commentator notes that a bad serve might prove decisive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' fits the tennis picture, where a bad serve is a fault, but it is the anagram signal; 'could be' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse comments are hostile, unfavourable ones, which is what critical remarks are.

clue.text: Crack force?

parts.note: read not as an elite unit but as police who deal with crack cocaine

explanation.surface: A crack force sounds like elite troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' means first-rate, but here it is the drug, and the force is a police team targeting it.
explanation.definitionFit: A police unit tackling narcotics would deal with crack cocaine among other illegal substances.

clue.text: Sail in such an important yacht

definitions.meaning: a small sail set above the topgallant on a square-rigger
the monarch's own vessel, such as Britannia, is called by this word

explanation.surface: A suggestion to go sailing aboard a very grand yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's monarch long had a state yacht, Britannia, described by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The topmost square sail on some masts has this name, and a yacht belonging to the sovereign carries the same adjective.

clue.text: Add nothing to pot at first, with two kings, in this?

definitions.text: Add nothing to pot at first, with two kings, in this?

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word pot

parts.note: nothing is zero, a round letter O
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ER is Edward Rex, the royal cipher of King Edward

explanation.surface: A card player holding a pair of kings declines to raise the stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a card game where you put chips in a pot and may hold two kings. ER is usually the Queen, but Edward VII's cipher was also ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game is played for a pot of stakes, in which a pair of kings is a decent hand.

clue.text: Expectant hero's narrow escape one regarded with contempt

parts.note: Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations
a narrow squeak is a close shave, a narrow escape

explanation.surface: A hero awaiting a baby has a close call, and is then scorned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expectant' suggests a coming baby; it points to Great Expectations. The possessive 's only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipsqueak is an insignificant, contemptible person.

clue.text: Satellite sent up for a lark, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the first commercial communications satellite, launched in 1965
someone who rises early, a morning person, called a lark

explanation.surface: A satellite is launched just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a lark' looks like 'for fun', but a lark is an early riser. The trailing D in the held text was a margin mark, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelsat I bore this nickname, and a lark is the songbird that rises with dawn, a byword for early risers.

clue.text: Up a tree? Girl there you'll find patient

parts.note: in a fir, up in a conifer tree
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl up a tree is told she will find a patient there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' reads as 'willing to wait' but is a noun: a sick person in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An infirmary is a hospital, the place where people receiving treatment are cared for.

clue.text: After conversion, act with spirit of the early fathers

indicators.note: conversion here means turning the letters of act and spirit into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone converted to the faith acts with the zeal of the early Church fathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' fits the religious picture but signals rearranging ACT and SPIRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Patristic studies concern the writings of the first Christian theologians, the Church Fathers.

clue.text: Agony for two lots of soldiers in race

indicators.note: in says the soldiers are put inside the race abbreviation

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Two groups of troops suffer agonies during a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe suffering, physical or mental.

clue.text: Sort of missile right for warship

parts.note: a cruise missile is a guided low-flying missile

explanation.surface: A missile suited to a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruiser is a fast, medium-sized warship.

clue.text: Feel fine, just a bit delicate

indicators.note: just a bit says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone says they feel well, only a little fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just a bit' reads as 'slightly' but asks for a small piece of FEEL FINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin features are small and dainty, like those of a fairy.

clue.text: Birds show alarm

definitions.meaning: small game birds of the partridge family; the plural is the same word
to cower or flinch in fear

explanation.surface: The birds display fright.
explanation.definitionFit: The game birds share their name with a verb meaning to shrink back in fear.

clue.text: Tree snake men beheaded

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: beheaded says the word men loses its head, its first letter

explanation.surface: A snake and some headless men by a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar with trembling leaves.

clue.text: Dance on stage in competition, making full circuit

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the dance word follows

parts.note: a round is one stage of a contest
to trip is to dance lightly, as in trip the light fantastic

explanation.surface: A dancer performs on stage in a competition and completes the whole circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance on stage' reads as a performance; 'on' in an across clue means the dance word comes after the competition word.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey out and back to the start completes a whole loop.

clue.text: Request piano to accompany heavy metal

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
lead is a heavy metal

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a piano to back a heavy metal band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' looks like rock music but is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to beg or ask earnestly.

clue.text: Looks for gold in river stretch

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite
to pan is to sift river gravel in a dish looking for gold

explanation.surface: A prospector searches for gold along a stretch of river.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide, open area, an unbroken extent of land or water.

clue.text: Place to store silver in school

indicators.note: in says the metal is put inside the school

parts.note: Stowe is an English public school in Buckinghamshire
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A school needs somewhere to keep its silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: Stowe is a well-known English private boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowage is room set aside for packing goods away, as in a ship's hold.

clue.text: Thoughtful type

explanation.surface: A considerate sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: A considerate person is caring towards others, and a sort or class of thing is the same word.

clue.text: Visionary has to stay in horribly seedy accommodation

indicators.note: in says the lingering word goes inside the scrambled letters
horribly says the letters of seedy are mangled into a new order

parts.note: to tarry is to linger or stay

explanation.surface: An idealist must put up with lodging in squalid digs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges SEEDY to S...EYED, which holds TARRY; 'accommodation' completes the picture of lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dreamy and idealistic, gazing at the stars, is a visionary.
